newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper, aluminium inventories to dip - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper, aluminium inventories to dip - trade.

text.p: Far East metal traders said London Metal Exchange (LME) copper and aluminium inventories will probably slip later on Friday.
Traders said copper stocks are likely to fall by between 2,000 to 5,000 tonnes, while aluminium stocks are seen dipping by between 5,000-10,000 tonnes, the traders said.
"I expect copper to be down by 2,000 tonnes," Vinod Kumar, managing director of Singapore-based Donald Mcarthy, said. Aluminium stocks should be "down by 5,000 tonnes," he added.
Another dealer for a European metal trading house said copper stocks appear headed for a 5,000-tonne fall while he estimated aluminium stocks would go down by 10,000 tonnes.
"Aluminium will most probably be 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes lower," he said, adding robust global demand has led to a steady drawdown in LME stocks.
Dealers said there were no reports of fresh shipments of copper moving into the LME's Singapore warehouse.
The volume of copper in the LME's warehouse in the city-state reached 54,720 tonnes in its stocks report on Tuesday, down 250 tonnes from the previous report last Friday.
Traders said they expect the level of LME copper stocks in Singapore to remain largely steady.
Three-month copper was seen by the trade at around US$2,401/406 a tonne at 0200 GMT, a touch firmer over the late quote in London on Thursday of $2,398/402 tonne.
Three-month aluminium was quoted by the same dealers at about $1,687/89 a tonne at 0200 GMT, almost unchanged from the kerb close in London yesterday of $1,689 a tonne.
